injuries.description: permanent pigmented and atrophic scars on left and right forearms and superior portions of both buttocks (multiple puncture and laceration scars described in disability findings)
injuries.body_part: left forearm; right forearm; superior portions of left and right buttock
source: (1) 20 mm x 4 mm transverse laceration scar at the ventral surface of the left forearm. The scare is flat and slightly pigmented.
(2) 8 puncture wounds of dot-like scars over the ventral and dorsal surface of left forearm all of which are pigmented.

(3) 9 puncture wounds over the dorsal of ventral surface of the right forearm, all are dot size and pigmented except one at the dorsal surface of the lower 1/5 which is larger measuring 15 x 20 cm, the surface is shiny.

(4) 3 scars of 10 mm x 5 mm, 10 mm x 60 mm, 10 mm x 10 mm at the superior portion of left buttock, two lateral and one medial. The medial scar is deeply pigmented, the lateral scars are slightly pigmented with a tropic surface.
(5) 2 round scars with diameter 5 mm x 10 mm at the superior portion of right buttock from lateral to medial, both are pigmented and flat.
The scars will be permanent and remain unsightly for life though some pigmentations may improve in about 2 – 3 years.
